title: Learn a new API in English
summary: Build a mental model and implementation plan directly from English API documentation.
learningObjectives: Explain an unfamiliar API and plan a safe first implementation without translation.

sections.title: Your mission
sections.body: Learn the fictional Pulse API well enough to plan a reliable integration.

sections.title: Pulse API quickstart
sections.content: Pulse accepts events through POST /v1/events. Each request needs an Authorization bearer token and a unique Idempotency-Key. Successful acceptance returns 202 with an event_id; processing is asynchronous. Query GET /v1/events/{event_id} until status is processed or failed. The API allows 60 requests per minute and returns 429 with Retry-After when the limit is exceeded. Reusing an idempotency key returns the original event rather than creating a duplicate.

exercises.question: Why must the client query event status?
options: A 202 response means processing is asynchronous.
correctAnswer: A 202 response means processing is asynchronous.
exercises.explanation: Acceptance and final processing are separate states.

performanceTask.title: Explain and plan the integration
performanceTask.scenario: A teammate will implement Pulse tomorrow and needs your English mental model and plan.
performanceTask.baselinePrompt: Read the quickstart once, hide it, then explain how the API works and outline implementation without translating it.
performanceTask.performancePrompt: Write 120–180 words: request lifecycle, idempotency, rate-limit behavior and a four-step implementation/test plan.
performanceTask.modelResponse: Pulse accepts an authenticated event and returns 202 because processing continues asynchronously. The client should generate one idempotency key per logical event, store the returned event_id and poll status until processed or failed. Reusing the same key prevents duplicate creation. I would first wrap POST and GET calls, then persist both identifiers. Next I would add bounded polling and handle 429 using Retry-After. Finally I would test duplicate submissions, failed processing and rate limiting before enabling the integration for real traffic.
performanceTask.retryPrompt: Rewrite the mental model in your own words and connect every implementation step to a behavior in the docs.
performanceTask.transferPrompt: A new Jobs API also returns 202, exposes job status and uses request tokens for deduplication. Produce a fresh mental model and implementation plan.
performanceTask.reviewPrompt: Read an unseen API quickstart once and explain lifecycle, safety mechanism, failure handling and first implementation plan from memory.

baseline.title: Pulse Events API
baseline.brief: Read once and build the request lifecycle from memory.

artifacts.title: Pulse quickstart
artifacts.content: POST /v1/events requires a bearer token and unique Idempotency-Key. Acceptance returns 202 with event_id; processing is asynchronous. Poll GET /v1/events/{event_id}. A 429 response includes Retry-After. Reusing a key returns the original event.

retry.title: Pulse reliability notes
retry.brief: Repair the weakest part of your mental model with focused evidence.

artifacts.title: Reliability contract
artifacts.content: 202 means accepted, not processed. Store event_id and one key per logical event. Poll until processed or failed. Respect Retry-After and do not create a new key for the same logical event.

transfer.title: Jobs API
transfer.brief: Unseen API with the same asynchronous function but different fields.

artifacts.title: Jobs quickstart
artifacts.content: POST /v2/jobs requires X-Request-Token and returns 202 with job_ref. Query GET /v2/jobs/{job_ref} until complete or failed. Duplicate tokens return the existing job. A 503 response includes Retry-In seconds.

review.title: Exports API
review.brief: Delayed retrieval from a new asynchronous API.

artifacts.title: Exports quickstart
artifacts.content: POST /exports accepts a report request and returns 202 with export_id. Supply Client-Request-Id to deduplicate. Poll /exports/{export_id}; download_url appears only at ready. On 429, wait for Retry-After before polling again.

trainingSource.title: Quanta Tasks API
trainingSource.content: POST /tasks requires Authorization and Request-Key. It returns 202 plus task_id. Poll GET /tasks/{task_id} until done or failed. Reusing Request-Key returns the original task. When the service returns 429, wait for Retry-After.

extractionItems.question: What does 202 mean here?
options: The task was accepted for asynchronous processing
extractionItems.correctAnswer: The task was accepted for asynchronous processing
extractionItems.feedback: Acceptance and final completion are separate states.

extractionItems.question: What prevents duplicates?
options: Reuse Request-Key for the same logical task
Generate a new key for every retry
extractionItems.correctAnswer: Reuse Request-Key for the same logical task
extractionItems.feedback: The request key identifies one logical operation.

extractionItems.question: How should 429 be handled?
extractionItems.feedback: The server supplies the backoff interval.
